name: Title bar and window controls
purpose: Application title, command centre and window actions.
strategy: Preserve native window integration; change product identity deliberately.

name: Activity Bar
purpose: Selects view containers such as Explorer and Extensions.
strategy: Hide or relocate through supported layout actions. It is not a list of every installed extension.

name: Primary Side Bar
purpose: Hosts active views such as files or a domain project tree.
strategy: Keep the container and choose its contents; hiding it does not disable views.

name: Secondary Side Bar
purpose: Provides a second area for views.
strategy: Candidate location for an inspector; a scientific property inspector must still be implemented.

name: Editor area and groups
purpose: Holds tabs, split groups, text editors and custom editors.
strategy: Keep the editor infrastructure even when a custom domain document dominates.

name: Panel container
purpose: Hosts Terminal, Output, Problems and other views.
strategy: Hide the container without assuming its services stop.

name: Status Bar
purpose: Shows state and short actions.
strategy: Contribute domain status and remove clutter through layout choices.

name: Commands, menus and keybindings
purpose: Dispatches actions independently of their visible button.
strategy: Do not remove command infrastructure to hide menu entries.

name: Notifications and progress
purpose: Reports progress, errors and questions.
strategy: Retain failure reporting and accessible alternatives in every profile.

name: Layout and view registration
purpose: Coordinates visibility, focus and size of workbench parts.
strategy: Treat as foundation, not as a removable ribbon.

name: File Explorer and file operations
purpose: Browse, open, rename and organize workspace resources.
strategy: A domain tree may supplement it; file services remain necessary when the tree is hidden.

name: Search across files
purpose: Finds text across workspace resources.
strategy: Separate global search from finding text within an editor.

name: Source Control interface
purpose: Presents change sets supplied by providers.
strategy: Separate provider UI from the bundled Git extension and an installed Git executable.

name: Run and Debug
purpose: Drives debug sessions through adapters.
strategy: Adapter licensing and terminal-backed launches require separate review.

name: Tasks and problem matchers
purpose: Runs configured processes and associates output with problems.
strategy: Observed dependency on terminal services; do not remove terminal while claiming task parity.

name: Integrated terminal
purpose: Shell sessions, process interaction and extension terminal API.
strategy: Hiding the panel leaves terminal APIs available. Exclusion needs a dedicated experiment.

name: Output and logs
purpose: Named text channels for tools and extensions.
strategy: A useful low-complexity interface for a domain engine; distinct from an interactive shell.

name: Problems and diagnostics
purpose: Collects diagnostic messages and locations.
strategy: Domain validation can reuse diagnostics rather than create a second error system.

name: Extensions manager
purpose: Lists and manages extensions.
strategy: Hiding this view does not remove the extension host or prevent installation through other routes.

name: Extension hosts and API bridge
purpose: Loads extensions and mediates their API access.
strategy: Retain for domain extensions. Desktop, web and remote hosts have different capabilities.

name: Settings and keybinding editors
purpose: Exposes configuration and shortcuts.
strategy: Defaults do not enforce a restriction; user and workspace overrides must be considered.

name: Themes and icon themes
purpose: Changes colours and icons through supported contributions.
strategy: Use theme tokens. Arbitrary workbench DOM/CSS changes are not a supported extension mechanism.

name: Workspaces and folders
location: Explorer, recent items and window state
purpose: Manages workspace identity and multi-folder configuration.
strategy: Keep separate from the scientific project format and its migration rules.

name: Unsaved documents and backup
purpose: Tracks document lifecycle and recovery.
strategy: Preserve save, revert, dirty-state and recovery contracts when adding domain editors.

name: Webviews and messaging
purpose: Hosts specialized HTML interfaces such as plots.
strategy: Requires message contracts, resource policy, keyboard and theme integration.

name: Custom document editors
purpose: Connects a domain file to a specialized editor provider.
strategy: Use the document lifecycle; test undo, save, restore and multiple views.

name: Notebook workbench
purpose: Hosts cell-based documents, execution and outputs.
strategy: Controller, renderer and format provider are separate components; do not equate this with Jupyter availability.

name: Testing interface
purpose: Displays tests provided by extensions.
strategy: Useful for reproducibility checks, but optional domain UI needs assessment.

name: Outline and symbol navigation
purpose: Navigates document structure from providers.
strategy: Could expose model structure when a provider has meaningful symbols.

name: Timeline and history views
purpose: Shows history supplied by providers.
strategy: A possible provenance entry point; scientific reproducibility needs richer records.

name: Workspace Trust
purpose: Coordinates trust state used by execution-related features.
strategy: Do not treat hiding trust prompts as disabling arbitrary execution. Audit trust providers before changes.

name: Accessibility and signals
purpose: Provides accessible navigation and feature support.
strategy: Preserve keyboard access and screen-reader behaviour; assess each custom view.

name: Accounts and authentication
purpose: Connects extensions to authentication providers.
strategy: Public API presence does not supply credentials or permission to reuse a hosted service.

name: Settings Sync
purpose: Synchronizes user state through configured services.
strategy: Service operation and account entitlement are separate from open-source client code.

name: Remote workbench plumbing
purpose: Connects a workbench to remote resources and extension hosts.
strategy: Do not assume Microsoft Remote extensions or server distribution rights carry over.

name: Chat and agent interfaces
purpose: User interfaces and orchestration for assistant workflows.
strategy: Model access, provider extensions and credentials are separately governed. Disabling one view is not removal of all AI code.

name: MCP integrations
purpose: Connects configured tool servers to supported workflows.
strategy: Include in the modern surface inventory; review execution and provider dependencies.

name: Application updates
purpose: Checks for and coordinates application updates.
strategy: A branded application needs its own release channel, signing and rollback policy.

name: Telemetry client contributions
purpose: Instrumentation integrated with product services.
strategy: Audit endpoints and extension telemetry separately; hiding UI has no effect.

name: User profiles
purpose: Separates groups of user configuration.
strategy: VS Code user profiles are not this project's build manifests; avoid conflating the two.

name: Agent Sessions window
purpose: Additional agent-oriented window in this development snapshot.
strategy: Audit independently before promising a classic-workbench-only distribution.
